title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, carried over from the previous page: X is a compact Riemann surface. The primes on X' are now dropped ('On laisse tomber dorénavant les \' des X !!'). X carries marked points (a_i), i in I, and a family of mutually disjoint closed conformal disks D_i, with D_i surrounding a_i. 'OPS' means 'on peut supposer': X connected and I non-empty.

Step 1. Form the bordered surface X* = X \ ∪_i D̊_i, obtained by removing the open disks. It inherits a conformal structure, and its boundary is the union of the circles ∂D_i.

Step 2. Grothendieck asserts that X* carries a canonical metric of constant curvature. It can be normalised to total area 1. It is 'strictly' canonical in the hyperbolic cases, i.e. all (g,ν) except g=0 with ν = card I in {1,2}. In the hyperbolic cases the boundary is geodesic. In modern terms this is the uniformisation of a bordered Riemann surface: double X* along its boundary, take the hyperbolic metric on the double, and the boundary becomes a union of closed geodesics.
- The exceptional case g=0, ν=2 is an annulus. It has the flat cylinder metric |dz|/|z|, which also has geodesic boundary.
- The exceptional case g=0, ν=1 is a disk. Here no Aut-invariant constant-curvature metric with geodesic boundary exists. The diagonal marginal note seems to flag exactly this trouble ('il y a un ennui ... disque ou une couronne').

Step 3. In every case each boundary circle receives a canonical 'structure torique' from the Riemannian structure. This is arc length rescaled to total length 1, i.e. a structure of oriented torsor under R/Z (equivalently U(1)).

Step 4. Each circle ∂D_i receives a second toric structure from the disk side. Uniformise (D_i, a_i) to (unit disk, 0); this is unique up to rotation, so the angle on ∂D_i is well defined up to translation. Equivalently, it is the harmonic measure of ∂D_i seen from a_i.

Step 5. The proposed restriction: require the two toric structures on each ∂D_i to coincide. The next page calls such disk systems 'admissible'. It reformulates them as: X is obtained from X* by 'bouchage de trous par des disques canoniques', i.e. capping each geodesic boundary circle with a standard disk glued by normalised arc length = angle. The next page then asks (Question 8) how admissibility compares with D_i being geodesic disks for a canonical (Bergman or hyperbolic) metric on X.

Purpose: this is a step toward a 'surgery' calculus on conformal surfaces with marked points and disks, for cutting and regluing, in the spirit of the Teichmüller tower of the Esquisse.

Implicit consequence (true, and pointed to on the next page):
- The rotation ambiguity is absorbed by Aut(D, 0).
- The welding map along an analytic geodesic is real-analytic, so the glued conformal structure is unique.
- Hence admissible data (X, a_i, D_i) correspond bijectively to bordered surfaces X* of type (g,ν).
- Dimension count: the hyperbolic bordered moduli have real dimension 6g−6+3ν, versus 6g−6+2ν for (X, a_i). So the ν extra real parameters are essentially the boundary lengths, i.e. the 'sizes' of the disks.
errors: The 'canonical metric with geodesic boundary' claim fails as stated for the disk case (g=0, ν=1). A disk has no Aut-invariant constant-curvature metric with geodesic boundary, so the boundary toric structure from the X* side is not canonical there. Grothendieck seems to notice this himself in the marginal note ('ennui ... disque ou une couronne').
Minor: 'volumes soit 1' should read 'volume soit 1'. Normalising the area to 1 conflicts with fixing the curvature at −1, but since only the normalised boundary measure matters, this is harmless.

ideas.what: Canonical constant-curvature metric with geodesic boundary on a compact bordered Riemann surface, via the Schottky double and uniformisation
ideas.modern_name: Uniformisation of bordered Riemann surfaces / hyperbolic metric with geodesic boundary

ideas.what: Boundary circles carry a canonical R/Z-torsor ('toric') structure from normalised hyperbolic arc length, or from harmonic measure on the disk side
ideas.modern_name: Canonical boundary parametrisations (up to rotation) of bordered surfaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Segal's CFT formalism (late 1980s) and in Huang's / Vafa's sewing with local coordinates

ideas.what: Admissible disk systems: matching the two toric structures, so that X = X* capped by canonical disks; admissible systems correspond bijectively to bordered hyperbolic surfaces
ideas.modern_name: Conformal welding / capping along parametrised boundaries (Segal-type sewing with canonical parametrisations)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Segal (1987), Vafa, Huang (1990s) for the sewing formalism; the specific hyperbolic-arc-length choice is not standardly attributed
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions surgery and the Teichmüller tower only in general terms

missed.claim: Grothendieck defines a canonical way to equip a marked Riemann surface with disjoint disks whose boundaries carry matching parametrisations. The device is hyperbolic arc length on the geodesic boundary of X* equalling harmonic measure from the centre. Admissible disk systems are thereby parametrised by bordered hyperbolic surfaces (boundary lengths as extra moduli). This anticipates the parametrised-boundary sewing formalism later used in CFT (Segal) and vertex-algebra geometry (Huang), but with a distinguished, metric-canonical choice of parametrisation. He also asks how admissibility compares with geodesic disks for the hyperbolic or Bergman metric; this question was apparently never pursued.
missed.quote: en exigeant que les deux structures toriques sur chaque ∂D_i (provenant soit de D_i, soit de X*) coïncident
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a canonical section of the infinite-dimensional sewing data (Segal's category) over the finite-dimensional bordered Teichmüller spaces. It also relates to work on capping hyperbolic surfaces with geodesic boundary (e.g. Mondello, Do), and possibly to a surgery-based construction of the Teichmüller tower as envisioned in the Esquisse.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is classical: uniformisation with geodesic boundary, and conformal welding. The specific 'admissibility' notion as a canonical capping device for a surgery calculus, predating Segal's formalism, is a modest unpublished detail of Grothendieck's 1983-84 programme. It is not a new theorem.
transcription_corrections: 'X^* = X \cup \bigcup_i \mathring{D}_i' should be 'X^* = X \setminus \bigcup_i \mathring{D}_i' (complement of the open disks).
'les volumes soit 1' is likely 'le volume soit 1'.
The marginal note likely begins 'il y a un ennui dans le cas où ...' and refers to the disk or annulus ('couronne') exceptional cases.
